title: feat(app-shell): Access is the fourth Studio pillar segment; the More overflow retires (objectui#12452)
body:
Fixes #12452
Clause-②: no

Part of the Studio layout redesign, epic objectui#12446, decision A: the maintainer's 2026-10-15 ruling, recorded on the card (comment 6188627851) and on the epic (comment 6188626991). Implemented in session `https://claude.ai/code/session_01SJn1GEkrbbBQkhGC26wEDw`.

## What

- The Studio shell header's segmented control reads **Data · Automations · Interfaces · Access**. Access is the fourth entry of `PILLARS`. It has the `Shield` glyph the overflow entry had, the same 28 px segment, the same narrow-viewport rule (an icon below the 1280 px design width, with the name kept in the accessible name and tooltip), and the same leave guard (`confirmLeavePillar`) as every other pillar link.
- `OVERFLOW_PILLARS`, the More popover, its `studio-nav-more` test id and the `engine.studio.more` string are removed. The string came out of the en and zh blocks of `metadata-admin/i18n.ts`, the only tables that had it: a grep of the whole tree finds it nowhere else, and the control key `engine.studio.pillar.access` still matches twice in the same file.
- Every pillar link now has `aria-current="page"` while its pillar is open. The overflow's Access link had that attribute. Moving Access into the row without it would have removed Access's only non-visual "you are here" signal. The artboards' header marks the open segment the same way.
- A comment at `PILLARS` keeps the objectui#11794 rule on record: if a second overflow pillar is ever added, More comes back and its trigger keeps the name More.
- The package-less scope (objectui#11553) still filters `PILLARS` down to its one pillar, so Access never appears there.

**Premise of ruling A, re-checked on `cf430cd` before building:** `OVERFLOW_PILLARS` held exactly one entry, `{ key: 'access', label: 'Access', Icon: Shield }`. The header was its only reader. `PILLAR_FOR_SURFACE_TYPE`, the deep-link channel and the pillar dispatch spell out `'access'` themselves and never read the list.

## Tests

- `StudioDesignSurface.moreKeepsName-11794.test.tsx` is retired along with the trigger, because the ruling supersedes it for More. It is replaced by `StudioDesignSurface.accessSegment-12452.test.tsx`, which pins:
  1. The four segments in order, each a link to its pillar, with no trigger of any kind next to them. The Access glyph is compared against lucide's own `Shield`.
  2. Access is active (current page, the active segment tokens, an icon in the primary color) under two package ids, `app.objectstack.hotcrm` and `com.acme.app`, with Interfaces open as the control.
  3. Leaving an unsaved pillar through Access asks exactly as leaving it through Data does: cancel keeps the author and the edit, confirm lands on Access, and a clean departure through Access never asks. The unsaved edit is an Interfaces nav edit, because Interfaces is the only pillar besides Access that reports one. It stays unsaved because the test holds the package list in flight, the same window `navEditClosesOnReadOnly-11167` uses.
- `StudioDesignSurface.pillarNavGuard.test.tsx`: its helper used to click More and then Access inside the menu; it now clicks the Access segment. No assertion changed.
- `StudioDesignSurface.packageLessFlows-11553.test.tsx`: the line that asserted there is no More trigger now asserts there is no Access link, which is what that line was guarding.

### Ablation, run once on the new pin

The suite resolves the surface from source, so no build was involved. Both mutations went through objectstack's `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`: the anchor hit once, the blob changed, and the file was restored to the HEAD blob with `git diff HEAD` empty. Both ran on `36254fe`.

| Mutation | New pin | pillarNavGuard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The Access link skips the leave guard (`p.key !== 'access' &&` inserted before `confirmLeavePillar()`) | The guard case goes red with `expected "vi.fn()" to be called 2 times, but got 1 times`; the other 5 stay green | 7 of 7 green: no older test catches a guard lost on Access alone |
| Access removed from `PILLARS` | 6 of 6 red | 3 of 7 red (the cases that click Access) |

## Evidence, pinned to `13afa58`

Measured on `13afa58`, the final head:

- `pnpm exec vitest run` on `accessSegment-12452`, `pillarNavGuard`, `accessGuard`, `packageLessFlows-11553`, `zhPillarNames-11801` and `createAppOpensInterfaces-11794`: `Test Files 6 passed (6)`, `Tests 44 passed (44)`.
- `pnpm check:i18n-keys`, `check:i18n-drift`, `check:i18n-dead-keys` and `check:i18n-designer-parity` all exit 0. The drift gate reports the designer table as `0 key(s) added, 1 removed`. The card asked for `pnpm check:i18n`, but no script by that name exists: `pnpm check:i18n` answers `Command "check:i18n" not found`, so the four families above stand in for it.
- `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` exits 0 (1 changeset declared). `check-changeset-no-major`, `check:new-line-citations` (0 new citations), `check:changeset-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals` and `check:test-path-roots` all exit 0.

Measured on `36254fe`. The only commits after it add the changeset and the two PNGs, so the code under test is identical:

- Every `StudioDesignSurface.*.test.tsx` file plus `metadata-admin/studio-locale.i18n.test.tsx`, in three batches: 77 files, 519 tests, all passed.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell run type-check` exits 0. `tsconfig.test.json` lists the three edited or new test files.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell run build` exits 0, with dist completeness verified. It was built on top of its 28-package dependency closure, which was also built.
- `eslint` on the five touched source and test files reports 0 errors. The 18 warnings were already on `cf430cd`, and none falls in a changed hunk.

The full farm is CI's job; see this PR's check runs.

## Screenshots

These are 1280 x 900, the same region as the artboard PNGs and the skeleton's before pair. They show HotCRM's Access pillar in the local console, run on my own stack (hotcrm `objectstack dev --fresh` on port 4152, console on port 5252).

- After, light: `docs/design/studio-redesign/after/12452-header-light.png`
- After, dark: `docs/design/studio-redesign/after/12452-header-dark.png`
- Before, the skeleton at `cf430cd` with More active in the header: `docs/design/studio-redesign/after/skeleton-access-light.png` and `skeleton-access-dark.png`

## Deviation list

- The pillar nav matches the header in every artboard (`access.html`, `data-records.html` and the rest): four 28 px segments in a 3 px padded muted track, with the open one on the card surface, its icon in the primary color and `aria-current` set. **No deviation in this card's region.**
- Elsewhere in the same frame the screenshots differ from `access.png`. These regions belong to other cards and this PR does not touch them:
  - The app chip shows a Read-only badge, because `objectstack dev` serves HotCRM read-only. The read-only posture is objectui#12453.
  - The Access body is one stacked page, not five tabs; that is objectui#12456.
  - Changes shows no count and Publish is an outline button, because the fresh database holds no drafts.

## Outside the claim's file surface

The claim names the surface, the More test, `i18n.ts`, the screenshots and the changeset. Two more test files read the retired trigger, and both get test-only edits:

- `StudioDesignSurface.pillarNavGuard.test.tsx`: acceptance 4 says this test must stay green, and its helper opened More. It cannot stay green once More is gone unless that helper changes.
- `StudioDesignSurface.packageLessFlows-11553.test.tsx`: without the edit, one of its assertions would have become vacuous.

When this was pushed, no open PR touched either file, and both sibling branches (objectui#12450, objectui#12454) were still at `cf430cd`.

## Acceptance notes

- The comment just above the shell header (it opens with "`overflow-x-auto` — none of Package/pillars/Publish shrink") still describes the scrolling strip that objectui#12459 retired. I left it alone because it is outside this card's region. Carrier: none.

- [x] Adds no product-specific widget, dialog, hook or string (see AGENTS.md › Product-neutral renderer)
